QuitérIA is a feminist artificial intelligence system developed for the Instituto AzMina's [Elas no Congresso](https://www.elasnocongresso.com.br/) project. It helps analyse, classify and assess Brazilian legislative proposals that affect women, girls and LGBTQIAPN+ people.

The system combines public legislative data, natural language processing and a dataset built through years of specialist human evaluation. It identifies thematic categories and estimates whether proposals may advance or threaten gender rights. Human review remains part of the process: the model supports analysis and does not replace political, legal or contextual judgement.

## My contribution

I worked on the **development and architecture of the system**, including the AI and data-modelling components that connect legislative data, model training, classification and validation.

## Technical approach

- Data collected from public APIs of the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies and Federal Senate.
- Portuguese-language NLP models based on BERTimbau.
- Multi-label thematic classification across ten areas of gender policy.
- A second model to assess whether proposals are favourable or unfavourable to monitored rights.
- Human validation and iterative retraining to identify errors and reduce blind spots.
- Open code, documentation and methodology whenever possible.

## Recognition

- **World Summit Awards Brasil 2026** — Government and Citizen Engagement.
- **VIII Prêmio Cláudio Weber Abramo de Jornalismo de Dados 2026** — Innovation and Experimentation. The jury highlighted the use of AI to organise large volumes of public data without replacing human analysis, with open code and specialist oversight.
